title: "What is the penalty for constraining the wings to sweep backwards?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 120.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 30.0
PROBE_POOL = 30.0
PROBE_SPENT = 17.2

res = optimize_full_glider(verbose=False, min_sweep=0)
sink_rate = res["sol"].value(res["sink_rate"])
sweep = res["sol"].value(res["sweep"])

sink_rate_baseline = 0.277 # from 2026-09-16-01-what-sink-rate-is-achieved-when-all-geometry-parameters-are-optimized.qmd
```

::: {.hero-pair}
[`{python} f"{sink_rate_baseline:.3f}"`]{.hero-value}
[unconstrained sink rate (m/s)]{.hero-label}

[`{python} f"{sink_rate:.3f}"`]{.hero-value}
[constrained sink rate (m/s)]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Constraining the leading edge sweep to be positive results in an optimal sweep that hits the bound exactly at `{python} f"{sweep:.1f}"`°. The sink rate increases only slightly, from `{python} f"{sink_rate_baseline:.3f}"` m/s in [the unconstrained optimization](2026-09-16-01-what-sink-rate-is-achieved-when-all-geometry-parameters-are-optimized.qmd) to `{python} f"{sink_rate:.3f}"` m/s.
